title: Colors All Around
bigQuestion: How do we name the colors we see in Spanish?

story.title: Painting a Rainbow
story.kicker: Two friends paint a rainbow and name every stripe in Spanish.
paragraphs: Sofía and Marcos have a big sheet of paper. They have paint and brushes too. "¡Vamos a pintar un arcoíris!" says Sofía. That means "Let's paint a rainbow!"
Marcos paints the top stripe. "*Rojo*," he says. That means red. Sofía paints the next one. "Anaranjado," she says. That means orange. Then comes amarillo, yellow like the sun.
Next they paint verde, green like grass. Then azul, blue like the sky. Last comes morado, purple like grapes. The rainbow is done!
Sofía's grandma looks at it. "¡Qué bonito!" she says. That means "How pretty!" She points to each stripe. The kids name every color in Spanish.
story.think: What is your favorite color? Can you find something that color in the room?

lessons.title: Red, Blue, Yellow
lessons.mainIdea: Rojo is red, azul is blue, and amarillo is yellow.
reading: Look at a fire truck. It is *rojo* (red). Look up at the sky on a sunny day. It is *azul* (blue).
Now look at a banana. It is *amarillo* (yellow). Say it slowly: a-ma-ri-llo. The ll sounds like y.
Red, blue and yellow can mix to make many other colors. They are a good place to start.

words.d: red — like a fire truck or a strawberry
blue — like the sky on a sunny day
yellow — like a banana or the sun

look.title: Three Balloons
look.text: Picture three balloons. The first balloon is red: rojo. The second balloon is blue: azul. The third balloon is yellow: amarillo. They float up into the sky.
look.prompt: Point to something red in your room. Say rojo.

check.why: Azul means blue, like the sky.
A banana is yellow, and yellow is amarillo.

check.q: How does the ll in amarillo sound?
check.why: In Spanish, ll sounds like y: a-ma-ri-yo.

lessons.title: Green, Orange, Purple
lessons.mainIdea: Verde is green, anaranjado is orange, and morado is purple.
reading: Grass and leaves are *verde* (green). A frog is often verde too. So is a green crayon.
An orange is anaranjado (orange). The fruit and the color have almost the same name! La naranja is the fruit.
Grapes can be *morado* (purple). Mix red and blue paint, and you get morado. Try it!

look.title: Mixing Paint
look.text: Put a drop of azul paint on your paper. Add a drop of amarillo. Mix them with your brush. Now it is verde! Red and yellow make anaranjado. Red and blue make morado.
look.prompt: What two colors make verde? Say them in Spanish.

check.q: Red and blue paint make which color?
check.why: Red and blue make purple, which is morado.

check.q: Which word names the color orange?
check.why: Anaranjado is orange. It sounds like la naranja, the fruit.

lessons.title: Pink, Black, White
lessons.mainIdea: Rosado is pink, negro is black, and blanco is white.
reading: A pig in a picture book is often *rosado* (pink). Some people also say rosa for pink.
Snow is *blanco* (white). A night sky with no moon is *negro* (black). So is a crow.
A zebra has two colors. It is blanco and negro. Can you think of other things that are black and white?

look.title: At the Zoo
look.text: Look at the zoo. A zebra stands by the fence. It is blanco and negro. A flamingo stands in the water. It is rosado. A big bird flies over. It is negro.
look.prompt: Name something at home that is blanco.

check.why: Milk is white, and white is blanco.
A flamingo is pink, which is rosado.

lessons.title: Brown: Café or Marrón
lessons.mainIdea: Brown can be café or marrón. Both are right.
reading: Look at a tree trunk. It is brown. Many people in Mexico say *café* for brown. Café is also the word for coffee!
Other people say *marrón* for brown. Both words are right. Different places use different words.
Your friends from different families may say it different ways. Listen and learn both!

words.d: brown — also the word for coffee
brown — another word many people use

look.title: The Puppy
look.text: A puppy runs in the park. His fur is brown. Ana says, "Es café." Luis says, "Es marrón." They are both right! The puppy wags his tail.
look.prompt: Find something brown. Say its color two ways.

check.q: Which two words can mean brown?
check.why: Café and marrón both mean brown.
Café is brown, and it is also the word for coffee.

check.q: Ana says café and Luis says marrón for the same dog. Who is right?
check.why: Both words mean brown. Different people use different words.

lessons.title: Asking ¿De Qué Color Es?
lessons.mainIdea: ¿De qué color es? means what color is it?
reading: Your friend holds up a ball. You ask, "¿De qué *color* es?" That means "What color is it?"
Your friend answers, "Es azul." That means "It is blue." Es means it is. Say es before the color.
Color is spelled the same in English and Spanish. In Spanish, say it co-LOR. Push on the last part.

words.d: it is — as in Es rojo (it is red)

look.title: Our Crayon Box
look.prompt: Which color has the most crayons? Say it in Spanish.

check.q: What does ¿De qué color es? mean?
check.why: ¿De qué color es? asks what color something is.
Es means it is, and verde means green.

check.q: A friend asks about a red apple. What do you say?
check.why: La manzana is a girl word, so red becomes roja: Es roja.

lessons.title: The Color Comes After
lessons.mainIdea: In Spanish, the color word comes after the thing: la manzana roja.
reading: In English we say the red apple. The color comes first. In Spanish, the thing comes first: *la manzana* roja.
Some colors change their end to match. El carro rojo, but la manzana roja. The o changes to a for la words.
English speakers often say la roja manzana. That is a mistake. Say the thing, then the color.

words.d: the apple — la manzana roja is the red apple
the balloon — el globo azul is the blue balloon

look.title: The Flag
look.text: Look at the flag of Mexico. It has three stripes. One stripe is verde. One is blanco. One is rojo. In the middle is an eagle. Now picture a blue balloon: el globo azul. The thing first, then the color.
look.prompt: Say a red apple in Spanish. Put the color last.

check.q: How do you say the red apple?
check.why: The color comes after the thing, and it ends in a to match la: la manzana roja.
In Spanish the thing comes first, then the color: el globo azul.

check.q: What colors are on the flag of Mexico?
check.why: Mexico's flag has green, white and red stripes.

review.q: The sky on a sunny day is what color?
review.why: The sky is blue, and blue is azul.

review.q: Blue and yellow paint make which color?
review.why: Blue and yellow make green, which is verde.

review.q: Which is right for the white cat?
review.why: The color comes after the thing: el gato blanco.

review.q: How do you ask What color is it?
review.why: ¿De qué color es? asks what color something is.
Snow is white, and white is blanco.
